feature_contract.goal: Prevent cross-device DirectGPU SafeEye, shared producer texture and GPU fence reuse when the host D3D11 device is replaced during Reset/recovery.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Host R32 DirectGPU A/B SafeEye recovery only; untouched gameplay HUD producer, DX11/DXVK, SkyGlow, FFB, and original compositor fallback.
feature_contract.special_work_evidence: The R32 cache hit previously required slot/frame generation/handles and dimensions, but omitted the D3D11 device identity; the SafeEyesOwnFrame fast path could return an old-device pair before a cache probe. Destructive regression mutations reproduce missing ownership invalidation.
trace_stages: D3D9Ex producer ring frame ID, slot generation, shared handles and game PID
Host R32 opened shared producer slots and A/B SafeEye GPU CopyResource plus fence
OpenXR two-eye projection sampling of the host-owned SafeEye SRVs after device recovery
subcomponents: Invalidate both producer-slot and inactive-eye per-device caches plus old query on host D3D11 device replacement
Invalidate active SafeEyes before fast identity reuse and publish device-owner identity for new source and inactive textures

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: All R32 source/inactive textures and fence belong to the current host device; reset restores a new-device pair before projection.
A matching frame ID/generation cannot bypass device-epoch synchronization; null device and old resources fail closed; unrelated HUD and fallback untouched.
Exact result SHA passes full Win32 DX9Ex host/game/package policy, Domain Isolation and Full Source Impact.

diagnosis.original_evidence: Existing R32OpenSharedSlot cache identity omitted host ID3D11Device and EnsureSafeFrameR32 checked SafeEyesOwnFrame before any device-epoch invalidation.
source_trace: Game writes ring frame ID and reused numeric shared handles after device lifecycle changes
R32 host shared slot reuses textures based on generation/handle alone, with stale inactive SafeEye and fence possible
OpenXR projection samples host SafeEye SRVs whose owning D3D11 device must match current renderer
diagnosis.root_cause: R32 host resource cache and SafeEye fast-path had no explicit host D3D11 device epoch barrier.
alternatives_rejected: Producer runGeneration protects game restarts but does not encode host graphics-device replacement.
A/B staging prevents timeout overwriting active frames but does not alone reject old-device SRVs.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: R32SyncDirectDeviceOwner resets active, inactive, shared and query resources before reuse; individual slot and inactive cache hits also check owner pointer.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: Existing R32 descriptor verifier extended with device identity and destructive old-SafeEye/old-fence/old-slot mutations.

runtime_note: Quest3/VDXR physical game/HMD recovery not exercised: exact-SHA Win32 compile, static mutation tests and source impact gates cannot establish headset correctness or frame pacing.
